name: Dumbbell Side Bend
summary: A unilateral core exercise performed standing with a dumbbell in one hand to train lateral flexion of the spine and strengthen the obliques.

setup: Stand upright with feet hip-width apart.
Hold a dumbbell in one hand at your side with an overhand neutral grip and arm fully extended.
Place your opposite hand behind your head or resting on your hip.
Brace your core and align your hips and shoulders facing straight forward.
steps: Lower the dumbbell down along your outer thigh by flexing your spine strictly to the weighted side.
Descend until you feel a deep stretch in the opposite oblique, keeping your hips stationary.
Contract the opposite side obliques and quadratus lumborum to pull your torso back upright.
Continue past neutral slightly to achieve a peak contraction on the working side before returning to the start.
Complete all repetitions on one side before switching the dumbbell to the opposite hand.
instructions.breathing: Inhale as you laterally flex toward the weighted side; exhale as you contract and pull your torso back upright.
cues: Move purely side-to-side between two panes of glass.
Keep your hips locked in place.

common_faults.fault: Holding dumbbells in both hands simultaneously.
common_faults.correction: Hold only one dumbbell at a time; holding two creates a counterweight that removes tension from the working muscles.

common_faults.fault: Twisting or leaning forward at the hips.
common_faults.correction: Maintain pure lateral flexion strictly in the frontal plane without rotating the torso or flexing forward.

common_faults.fault: Using momentum or excessive range of motion that compromises spinal control.
common_faults.correction: Move slowly through a controlled range of motion without jerking the weight up.

precautions: Avoid using excessively heavy loads that cause sudden lateral shearing forces on the lumbar spine.
